failures.evidence: Same single failure as the previous run, and it has now been adjudicated. Human ruling, journal seq 239 (re-applying seq 115, approver neil): 'the test over-asserts ... the contract never promised that, and it should not be changed to promise it -- an error body may legitimately differ between the two. Treat that failure as a test defect'; answers.route = 'author-tests'. The offending assertions are RedirectTest.java:336 and :339, assertEquals(postOnALiveCode.body(), postOnAnUnissuedCode.body()) and the DELETE pair, inside assertAll at RedirectTest.java:333. Surefire: expected <{"timestamp":"2026-08-11T01:35:30.761+00:00","status":405,"error":"Method Not Allowed","path":"/BCvnUPjblaA47bscIEQTqj"}> but was <..."path":"/ZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZz"}> — identical status and error, differing only in the echoed request path (caller-known) and a 3ms clock delta. The implementation matches openapi.yaml:123-124 note 2, 'Every other method on /{code} answers 405 from Spring's own dispatcher. No operation is declared for them', repeated at openapi.yaml:589. test-contract.json B106 says only 'refused identically whether or not the code resolves' and pointedly omits the 'byte for byte' / 'the same body' wording used by B104 and B107, so byte-equality is asserted matter the contract never promised. AC15 is not violated by the observed responses: nothing in them distinguishes a live code from an unissued one. Not an implementation defect — the code does what note 2 says.

summary: One failure out of 148 tests (21 classes, 0 errors), unchanged from the previous verify: RedirectTest.aMethodOtherThanGetOrHeadIsRefusedWithoutRevealingWhetherTheCodeExists. coverage_floor is purely downstream — surefire fails in the test phase so no jacoco.csv is written (jacoco.exec exists); routes_match_openapi passed 8/8. The previous triage classified this 'contract' and escalated; a human has since ruled (journal seq 239, re-applying seq 115): the test over-asserts by demanding byte-identical 405 bodies for a live and an unissued code, the contract never promised that, and the route is author-tests. I classify it 'test' at high confidence on that ruling plus B106's wording, which omits the 'byte for byte' language B104/B107 use. The repair is to assert what the contract does promise — 405 on both, and no signal distinguishing existence (e.g. same status, same error field, no Location) — not to delete the assertion or downgrade it to a status-only comparison, which would erase AC15 intent. If I am wrong, the thing to check is whether openapi.yaml:47 ('Every non-2xx response has the ApiError shape. The catalogue is closed') was meant to govern the dispatcher-produced 405 on the click surface; if a human reversed the seq 239 ruling and said it does, this flips to implementation and the closed catalogue gains a 405 row.
